extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in NLP/IR/HCI and patent attorneys interested in automating USPTO Office Action responses
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating systems (PARIS and LE-PARIS) to assist attorneys in generating timely, effective responses to USPTO Office Actions using an OA topics database, response templates, recommender systems, and LLM-based response generation, validated through multi-paradigm analyses and user studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and effectiveness of OA responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Timely and effective responses to Office Actions (OAs) are crucial for securing patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system's goal is to improve the timeliness and effectiveness of attorney OA responses; evaluation should measure time-to-response and whether responses successfully address OA issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: OA Topics Database construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction of an OA Topics Database
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build a structured database of Office Action (OA) topics that supports retrieval and recommendation; evaluate topic coverage, granularity, and usefulness to attorneys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructiveness of OA topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructiveness of OA topics (studies 1 and 2) using topic modeling and our proposed Delphi process
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether derived topics are actionable/constructive for drafting responses via quantitative topic modeling and qualitative Delphi expert review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response Templates development
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create and organize reusable response templates for common OA scenarios; evaluate template relevance, adaptability, and how much they reduce drafting effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommender Systems efficacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Efficacy of our proposed hybrid LLM-based recommender system tailored for OA responses (study 3)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure recommender accuracy, precision/recall of recommended topics/templates, relevance to the OA, and utility in speeding attorney workflows; the system is hybrid and LLM-enhanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM-based Response Generation quality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the quality of LLM-generated OA responses (study 4) across dimensions such as relevance, correctness, legal/technical adequacy, fluency, and need for human edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical value and impact on attorney performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems' practical value in real-world scenarios through user studies (study 5)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use user studies and longitudinal interaction data to measure impact on attorney performance metrics (e.g., efficiency, accuracy, reduced drafting time, user satisfaction) and real-world utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-paradigm evaluation using USPTO and longitudinal data
rubrics_metrics.description: Employed a multi-paradigm analysis using the USPTO Office Action database and longitudinal data based on attorney interactions with our systems over six years
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate systems across multiple data sources and study designs: large-scale OA datasets (USPTO) for quantitative evaluation and long-term interaction logs for longitudinal impact analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Achievement of key performance metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Both PARIS and LE-PARIS significantly achieve key metrics and have a positive impact on attorney performance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and report concrete 'key metrics' (e.g., response quality scores, recommendation accuracy, time savings, adoption rates) and demonstrate statistical improvements versus baselines.
